title: Classical training versus the dance field
summary: The Tio pupils went to dance music; Elgar says Dixieland demands real technique and trained musicians.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Do you remember who else played in the orchestra, the other clarinetists?
Louie Teo. Well, his brother was Lorenzo. Lorenzo was one of them. I don't remember the others.
Do you remember Alphonse Piku ever played? Who? Alphonse Piku.

Oh no, you see, those boys didn't go in for that type of... They had enough training on their instrument, but they didn't go in for that classical side. From the very beginning, they went into the dance field.

Yeah, and they stayed in that dance field. I had thought that Piku did some classical music too. I think somebody told me. We haven't interviewed him very much so far. We did have one interview with him.
He was qualified and capable of playing it if he wanted to, but he was more interested in the popular thing. Because as you well remember, at that time, the Dixonite music was just a thing.
Yes, yes. Of course, that's our main study is going to be in that type of music. Yeah. We're glad to get all of the classical background because all of that helped.
Oh my gosh, yes. It had much to do because until you know your instrument, such as those boys do, you can't be very successful in that Dixonite music because it calls for a lot of technique.
Most of them actually can read too. Oh yeah, sure. Oh yeah, sure.
Now, when you hear this outfit that's at the preview at Fran Jackson, you'll see just what I'm referring to. Every man in there is very thorough musician.
